# Studentplat

> Studentplat is a web platform for Italian university students to track their academic progress: study days, upcoming exams, passed exams with grades and credits (CFU), arithmetic and credit-weighted averages, and grade trends.

Important notes:

- All personal data (profile, exams, grades) is private and only visible after login. Agents cannot read user data without the user's own session; there is no public API.
- The interface is available in Italian (default) and English. The language is stored in the `lang` cookie and changed with a POST to `/lang`.
- Grades follow the Italian system: 1 to 30, plus "30 e lode" (30 cum laude, shown as "30L"), stored as 31 and counted as 31 in averages. A grade below 18 means the exam was not passed. Each attempt can also be "withdrawn or absent" (no grade) or a pass grade declined by the student.
- An exam is passed when it has an attempt with a grade of 18 or more that was not declined; each exam can be passed only once. A passed exam can no longer be scheduled or receive another result.
- Exams are a shared catalogue: the first user who creates an exam (name and credits) makes it available as a template to every other user, who adds it to their own transcript.

## Pages

- [Home](/): Public presentation of Studentplat and its features (logged-in users are redirected to the dashboard).
- [Login](/login): Log in and sign up (`/login?tab=register` opens the sign-up form).
- [Dashboard](/dashboard): Overview of the student's progress: degree programme and university, the next three planned exam sessions not yet passed (date, credits and days left, each linking to the calendar month), and credits earned out of the degree's total with a progress bar (login required).
- [Transcript](/dashboard/exams): The student's transcript ("Libretto"): every exam with credits, status (to take, passed with grade and date, not passed), planned exam session, lecturer, personal difficulty (easy, medium, hard, only if set) and number of attempts. Passed exams come first, in date order. Each exam expands to edit the lecturer and the personal difficulty, see and delete attempts, and open the calendar on the exam's month (login required).
- [Statistics](/dashboard/stats): Statistics on passed exams: arithmetic and credit-weighted averages (30L counts as 31), graduation base (weighted average x 110 / 30, one decimal), exams passed and still to take, credits earned out of the degree's total, highest and lowest grade, number of cum laude grades, grade distribution in bands (18-20, 21-23, 24-26, 27-29, 30, 30L), attempt outcomes (passed, withdrawn or absent, failed, declined) with the share of exams passed at the first attempt, and a chart of each passed exam's grade in date order with the cumulative weighted average (the same data is also in a table for screen readers). Without passed exams it links to the transcript (login required).
- [Calendar](/dashboard/calendar): Monthly calendar of the student's exam sessions and results (`?month=YYYY-MM`, default current month). Selecting a day lets the student schedule an exam from the shared catalogue, move an exam already in their transcript to that day, remove it from the day, create a new catalogue exam, or record the result of an exam on that day (grade 1-30 or 30L, withdrawn/absent, declined grade, notes). Scheduling, moving or creating an exam can also set its personal difficulty (optional; leaving it out keeps the one already saved). Days with a result show the grade; exams with a difficulty are marked with its colour (login required).
- [Profile](/dashboard/profile): Nickname, degree programme, university and total credits of the degree, with a link to the import page and a section to permanently delete the account after re-entering the password (not available to administrators; login required).
- [Import exams](/dashboard/profile/import): Two tabs (`?tab=passed`, default, and `?tab=planned`). Past exams adds past exam attempts to the transcript from a pasted JSON list; upcoming exams adds exams still to take to the transcript, with an optional planned date. Each tab shows the format description and a copyable example (login required, see below).
- Admin panel (`/admin`): reserved to site administrators; other users get a 404.

## Importing exams

The import page (`/dashboard/profile/import`, linked from the profile) has two tabs. Both accept a JSON array of 1 to 200 items, at most 100 KB; unknown fields are ignored.

### Past exams (`?tab=passed`)

Accepts a JSON array (1 to 200 items, at most 100 KB) of past attempts:

```json
[
  { "name": "Analisi matematica I", "cfu": 12, "date": "2025-02-10", "grade": 28, "teacher": "Mario Rossi", "difficulty": "hard" },
  { "name": "Programmazione", "cfu": 9, "date": "2025-06-20", "grade": "30L" },
  { "name": "Fisica", "cfu": 6, "date": "2025-07-01", "grade": 24, "rejected": true, "notes": "rifiutato" },
  { "name": "Chimica", "cfu": 6, "date": "2025-01-15", "grade": null }
]
```

- `name` (up to 150 characters) and `cfu` (whole number 1-30) identify the catalogue exam, case-insensitively; missing exams are created.
- `date`: `YYYY-MM-DD`, not in the future.
- `grade`: 1-30, `"30L"` or 31 for 30 cum laude, `null` for withdrawn or absent.
- Optional: `rejected` (true only with a grade of 18 or more), `teacher` (up to 150 characters), `difficulty` (`"easy"`, `"medium"`, `"hard"` or `null`, the student's personal difficulty for the exam), `notes` (up to 255 characters).
- Everything is validated first: if any item is invalid, or would pass an exam that is already passed (in the transcript or earlier in the list), nothing is saved and the errors are listed by row. Exact duplicates (same exam, date and grade) are skipped and counted.

### Upcoming exams (`?tab=planned`)

Adds exams still to take to the transcript:

```json
[
  { "name": "Analisi matematica II", "cfu": 9, "date": "2026-02-12", "teacher": "Lucia Bianchi", "difficulty": "hard" },
  { "name": "Basi di dati", "cfu": 9, "date": "2026-01-28" },
  { "name": "Sistemi operativi", "cfu": 12, "difficulty": "medium" },
  { "name": "Lingua inglese B2", "cfu": 3, "date": null }
]
```

- `name` and `cfu` as above; the same exam (case- and accent-insensitive name plus credits) can appear only once in the list.
- Optional: `date` (planned exam date `YYYY-MM-DD`, any valid date, or `null`), `teacher` (up to 150 characters), `difficulty` (`"easy"`, `"medium"`, `"hard"` or `null`).
- If any item is invalid nothing is saved. Exams already in the transcript are skipped and left unchanged (counted as already present).
